stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Fields K over S have a given map Spec(K)→S, with X(K)=Mor_S(Spec K,X).

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable
morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$. Then $f$ is universally injective
(in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable})
if and only if for all fields $K$ the map $X(K) \to Y(K)$ is injective.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable
morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
conclusions:
$f$ is universally injective
(in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable})
if and only if for all fields $K$ the map $X(K) \to Y(K)$ is injective.

reason: The universal-injectivity criterion for representable maps is equivalent to at-most-one lifting on every field-valued point. Base changes have K-valued points equal to fibre products of K-points, so injectivity for all fields is stable under all scheme tests and conversely detected by them.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Fields K over S have a given map Spec(K)→S, with X(K)=Mor_S(Spec K,X).

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the map $X(K) \to Y(K)$ is injective for every field $K$ over $S$
\item for every morphism $Y' \to Y$ of algebraic spaces over $S$
the induced map $|Y' \times_Y X| \to |Y'|$ is injective, and
\item the diagonal morphism $X \to X \times_Y X$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
conclusions: the map $X(K) \to Y(K)$ is injective for every field $K$ over $S$

for every morphism $Y' \to Y$ of algebraic spaces over $S$
the induced map $|Y' \times_Y X| \to |Y'|$ is injective, and
the diagonal morphism $X \to X \times_Y X$ is surjective.

reason: The field-valued-point injectivity criterion shows arbitrary base changes have injective underlying-point maps. Conversely any pair of K-valued lifts that agree in Y become equal over a common field extension and descend by the fpqc sheaf property. Surjectivity of the diagonal is equivalent to pointwise fibres having at most one point after all base changes.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Fields K over S have a given map Spec(K)→S, with X(K)=Mor_S(Spec K,X).

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is universally injective,
\item for every scheme $Z$ and any morphism $Z \to Y$ the morphism
$Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is universally injective,
\item for every affine scheme $Z$ and any morphism
$Z \to Y$ the morphism $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is universally injective,
\item there exists a scheme $Z$ and a surjective morphism
$Z \to Y$ such that $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is universally injective, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is universally injective.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
conclusions:
for every scheme $Z$ and any morphism $Z \to Y$ the morphism
$Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is universally injective,

for every affine scheme $Z$ and any morphism
$Z \to Y$ the morphism $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is universally injective,

there exists a scheme $Z$ and a surjective morphism
$Z \to Y$ such that $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is universally injective, and

there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is universally injective.

reason: Base-change permanence and fppf descent after a surjective scheme chart establish (1)–(4). However the source explicitly omits the equivalence of condition (5), the Zariski-local criterion, at line 3635.
